title: The Protocol of Halcyon Drift
premise: Sable Blackwood, an insurance investigator specializing in 'impossible accidents,' is dispatched to Halcyon Drift, a derelict station between two fleets on the brink of war, to price out its liabilities. There she discovers the colony's children share one recurring dream—a memory encoded in the station's reactor by a dead engineer, her own estranged mother, containing proof that both governments falsified the atrocity that started their feud. As the reactor's failsafe countdown ticks toward a burn that will erase the evidence and the station alike, Sable must choose between delivering her report, which would trigger the war both fleets want, and keeping her mother's final lie alive. She forges the report, sacrifices her career and her engagement to a fleet officer, and broadcasts the children's dream instead, forcing both admiralties to stand down at the edge of the burn.
about_author: Hazel Ashgrove is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses no one wanted to explain. She writes science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people who keep impossible systems running.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She closes a case on a freighter that 'spontaneously' vented itself, pocketing the truth to keep a widow's payout intact. Her firm, Meridian Assurance, assigns her to Halcyon Drift—a station both fleets officially claim doesn't exist. Beat: competence as armor; she's good at making disasters mean nothing.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The transit between the Concord and Verity fleets' space, where ships fly dark and radio silence is law. She reviews her file on Halcyon Drift: a reactor anomaly, forty-one residents, and a prior investigator who resigned mid-report. Beat: loneliness of the neutral corridor; first glimpse of the dream data in the telemetry.

chapters.title: Forty-One Souls
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, arriving at the station. The colonists are warm, evasive, and strangely synchronized—pausing at the same moments, glancing at the same ceiling. The children watch her like she's expected. Beat: uncanny welcome; the reader senses the colony is hiding something kind, not sinister.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Wren, age nine, station-born. She dreams of a woman in a reactor gallery singing numbers, and wakes with equations on her slate she can't write. The other children dream the same dream, same night, same numbers. Beat: wonder edged with fear; the dream feels like being trusted with something heavy.

chapters.title: The Prior Investigator
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She finds the resigned investigator, Odile Vann, running a noodle stand in the lower ring. Odile warns her: the reactor isn't failing, it's counting, and the station's charter is a forgery signed by someone with fleet-grade clearance. Beat: dread; the case is bigger than a liability assessment.

chapters.title: Mother's Signature
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The forged charter's engineer-of-record is Ilsa Blackwood—Sable's mother, dead eleven years, the reason Sable left the Concord fleet for insurance work. Emotional beat: fury and vertigo; the investigation just became personal, and Sable hates her mother a little for it.

chapters.title: Reactor Gallery
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, descending with the station's aging caretaker, Bram. The reactor hums a pattern she recognizes from her childhood—her mother's habit of singing primes while she worked. A failsafe counter reads 19 days. Beat: grief made mechanical; the station is her mother's last message, addressed to whoever finally came.

chapters.title: The Atrocity File
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The children, comparing dreams, realize the numbers are coordinates and dates. Wren sneaks into the archive with the dream's key and opens a sealed file: the Callas Incident, the massacre both fleets blame on each other, with sensor logs proving a third ship fired. Beat: loss of innocence; the children now carry the war's real secret.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing the logs, she confirms both governments knew the truth and buried it—war is profitable, peace would require admitting the shared lie. Her firm's liaison, Corven, arrives early and asks pointed questions. Beat: cynicism hardening into resolve; Sable understands why her mother hid the evidence here.

chapters.title: The Man from the Fleet
chapters.summary: POV of Captain Elias Renn, Sable's former fiancé, now Concord fleet intelligence, ordered to 'secure' Halcyon Drift before the reactor event. He requests Sable by name, telling himself it's operational, not personal. Beat: duty versus love established; he's a good man carrying out a bad order.

chapters.title: Countdown at Dinner
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The colonists throw a station-wide dinner, and Sable realizes they know about the countdown and have chosen to stay—Halcyon Drift is home, not a liability. Wren shows Sable the dream, child to investigator. Beat: belonging; Sable's professional detachment cracks for the first time.

chapters.title: Corven's Report
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corven intercepts her draft assessment and rewrites it: Halcyon Drift to be declared a total loss, station and colonists written off as 'acceptable exposure.' Sable realizes her firm is the fleets' laundering mechanism. Beat: betrayal; the paperwork was always the weapon.

chapters.title: What Odile Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, flashback chapter. Eleven years ago, Odile and Ilsa Blackwood discovered the Callas truth together; Ilsa encoded it in the reactor's dream-broadcast and forged the charter to buy the station time. Odile resigned and stayed to raise the children inside the dream. Beat: the mother's sacrifice revealed; the lie is a cradle.

chapters.title: Elias Docking
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Renn's ship arrives; they meet as adversaries wearing old tenderness. He offers her extraction and her career back if she walks away before the burn. She refuses. Beat: love against duty, both choosing their sides with broken hearts.

chapters.title: The Children's Broadcast
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The children, guided by the dream's final verse, prepare to transmit the Callas logs on the reactor's carrier wave—visible to both fleets. Bram and the colonists vote to help, knowing it marks them. Beat: courage of the small; the colony stops hiding.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corven seizes the station's comms and detains the colonists; the countdown drops to 4 days as the reactor responds to tampering. Sable is confined to quarters with a termination clause on her contract. Beat: darkest hour; the system she served turns its full weight on the innocent.

chapters.title: The Forged Assessment
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She escapes via the maintenance routes her mother designed, reaches the records office, and forges the report Corven wanted—declaring the reactor evidence destroyed, the station worthless—buying the fleets a reason to disengage. Beat: inheritance; she commits her mother's crime knowingly, as an act of love.

chapters.title: Renn's Choice
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Ordered to fire on the station's antenna array, Renn reads the raw dream transmission his own daughter-age crewman has been dreaming since arrival. He refuses the order and turns his ship's shields to cover the broadcast. Beat: the second defection; duty breaks where love and truth converge.

chapters.title: The Burn
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren's alternating POV, climax. With 90 seconds left, Sable sings her mother's primes into the reactor's console—the final key—and the failsafe redirects: the reactor burns its evidence skyward in a single visible flare both fleets witness, the dream broadcast riding the light. Beat: sacrifice transfigured; the lie that held the fleets apart dies in the same light as the truth.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Stand Down
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. In the flare's aftermath, both admiralties, their shared atrocity now public among their own crews who all dreamed it, halt hostilities. Corven is arrested by his own employers for creating exposure. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered by witnesses rather than courts.

chapters.title: Claims Settled
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, falling action. She's blacklisted by Meridian and quietly celebrated everywhere else; she and Renn, unengaged and unburdened, begin again slowly. The colonists rebuild; Odile finally serves noodles at a victory dinner. Beat: cost acknowledged; some losses are worth their price.

chapters.title: The Dream, Continued
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, coda. Months later the children still dream, but now the woman in the reactor gallery is singing to other stations—the code seeded itself across the long route. Wren, training as the station's new engineer, adds her own verse. Beat: inheritance fulfilled; the truth travels, and the next generation keeps the watch.
